s0c_definition.scope_note: DS1 validation check by SV1 (s0c_v1_check_ds1val.json): macro-F1 of C5 on the reconstructed beats 0.568057 over 9,523 beats; not re-measured and not used by any attack decision

s0c_observed_tensor.definition: What the edge holds after Rice decoding: the 46 dequantized values v = decode(body, scale)[0] of s0c_v1_ref.py (Rice is lossless, so the payload and v carry the same information). Attacker input: v as an NCL tensor [1, 46] in FP32
s0c_observed_tensor.edge_interpolation: x_c = decode(body, scale)[1], the 360 reconstructed samples; x_c is the input of the frozen model at the edge and the start of every composite from S0c
s0c_observed_tensor.implementation: SV3's runner may use a vectorized implementation for speed, but before any S0c number it must reproduce the reference outputs bit for bit (reduced values, q, FP16 scale, dequantized values, reconstructed samples, Rice body bytes) on the 20 golden beats and on every DS1 beat of the trial data (clean, rho0); any difference stops the S0c items before a number exists and is reported to SV1
s0c_observed_tensor.golden_check: Done on 2026-11-26 for the reference itself (source_bindings.s0c_definition.sv3_receipt_check); repeated by the runner for its own implementation

part_a_s9_logits_and_s0c.observed_tensor: s9 and s10 as v2 observed_tensor: z_s of checkpoint A computed one beat at a time, to_ncl with L = 1, registry v2 quantize_per_channel then dequantize_per_channel; the attacker input is the dequantized FP32 [C] vector (C = 32 at s9, 5 at s10). s0c: s0c_observed_tensor
part_a_s9_logits_and_s0c.logits_definition: The s10 tensor is the FP32 PyTorch output of the full checkpoint A on the normalized beat (classifier.4, 5 values N, S, V, F, Q), quantized like every other split: the nominal 15 B tensor (5 INT8 + 5 FP16) of table_iii. It stands for every logits vector the edge can compute from z_s with the FP32 reference tail it knows (threat_model.knows: tail weights)
part_a_s9_logits_and_s0c.kv260_logits: Not attacked: the KV260 INT8 logits (multiples of 0.125) are another function of z_s; omitting a variant can only leave Pi higher, so every Pi here stays an upper bound. Listed in limitations
part_a_s9_logits_and_s0c.golden_check: rho0 z_s9 and z_s10 of the 20 package A golden beats must equal golden/z_s9.npy and golden/z_s10.npy bit for bit (v2 golden_check extended to s9, s10); s0c: s0c_observed_tensor.implementation

attacks.B_naive: s9, s10: v2 attack_models.B_classifier.base.NC (MLP 128); s0c: v2 base.NCL (2 blocks, 64 channels, kernel 5) on [1, 46]. 3 seeds 20261030, 20261031, 20261101. Per-beat log-probabilities on the test part are saved with the argmax predictions
attacks.A1: s9, s10: v2 attack_models.A1_decoder, seed 20261030. s0c: the training-free floor x_c and a trained refiner Conv1d(1, 16, 5) + ReLU, Conv1d(16, 16, 5) + ReLU, Conv1d(16, 1, 5) (padding 2) applied to x_c, MSE against the normalized x, seed 20261030, v2 A1 training settings; both reported, the headline is the one with the lower mean NRMSE on the attacker-validation part. Reported, not part of Pi

part_a_s9_logits_and_s0c.architecture: Base: the v2 trial capacity check (s0 mean bacc 0.8256 >= 0.80) decided 'base' for every split; it is not repeated and not revised. s0c uses the same base NCL family
part_a_s9_logits_and_s0c.reported: Per pair as v2 (Pi, CI95, seed range, per-seed results, session bacc, A1 metrics); Pi(s9) and Pi(s0c) are then also combined with B_composite in part b
part_a_s9_logits_and_s0c.names: Pi_v3(s9, rho0) and Pi_v3(s0c, rho0) after part b; Pi_logits = Pi of B_naive on the s10 tensor (no deeper split exists, so no composite)

reading_declared_before_run.Pi_logits_below_Pi_min: Pi_logits < 0.5: with this metric no offload configuration that keeps the logits computable at the edge (every s < 10 under rho0, and S0c) can reach Pi_min. Recorded as a property of the problem; Pi_min is NOT lowered
reading_declared_before_run.Pi_logits_at_least_Pi_min: Pi_logits >= 0.5: no such statement; Pi(s < 10) stays what its own measurements give
reading_declared_before_run.Pi_s9_at_least_Pi_min: Pi_v3(s9, rho0) >= 0.5: report to SV1, who reopens the bottleneck question (SV1 2026-11-19 section 3, last part)
reading_declared_before_run.Pi_s9_below_Pi_min: Pi_v3(s9, rho0) < 0.5: the bottleneck route stays closed
reading_declared_before_run.Pi_s0c: Pi_v3(s0c, rho0) is the privacy entry of the standard S0 in every table (SV1 2026-11-25 item 1(2)); the trial Pi(s0) of the full beat stays a trial number and is not substituted for it
reading_declared_before_run.action_set: Pi(s10) of the action set is 1 by construction (SV1 2026-11-19 section 5); Pi_logits never filters s10

part_b_B_composite.applies_to: rho0 (checkpoint A) only: every split shares one model, so the edge that receives z_s holds every op after s. Under rho1 each split is a different checkpoint whose deeper-split attackers do not exist; B_composite is not defined for rho1 in this version and Pi(s, rho1) stays B_naive
part_b_B_composite.argument: The edge that receives the observed tensor u_s at s can compute u_s' for any s' > s and run the attacker trained at s'. So the true Pi(s, rho0) cannot exceed Pi(s', rho0) except through the quantization error at s, and for S0c the information removed by the reduction to 46 values; the measured order 0.100 -> 0.068 reflects attacker weakness at shallow splits. This is the hypothesis part b measures; the trial value Pi(s0) = 0.183 is not used anywhere

sources_and_targets.pairs: Every (s, s') with s in source_splits, s' in target_splits, s' deeper than s (s0 and s0c are shallower than every target): 27 composite evaluations (6 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1)
sources_and_targets.attackers: s' in {2, 4, 5, 8}: the v2 trial attackers <s'>-rho0-attackers.pt (s0 is never a target); s' in {9, 10}: the part a attackers

computation.input: u_s = the observed tensor at s exactly as v2 observed_tensor (for s0: dequantized INT8 x, the 362 B payload); for s0c: x_c, the edge interpolation of the 46 values (s0c_observed_tensor)
computation.ops: frozen ops OPS[CUTS[s]:CUTS[s']] of checkpoint A (week3_sv2_common.CUTS), with CUTS[s0c] = CUTS[s0]; CPU, week3_sv2_common.configure; batched when s' <= 8, one beat at a time when s' >= 9; s9 sources enter as [N, 32] (to_ncl undone)
computation.quantization: z'_s' -> to_ncl -> quantize_per_channel -> dequantize_per_channel (registry v2), so the attacker sees the same kind of tensor it was trained on; the edge can do this itself
computation.standardization: Mean and std of the attacker-train part of the genuine u_s' (the statistics the s' attacker was trained with), recomputed with v2 attack_models.input_standardization
computation.prediction: Each of the 3 seeds' B attackers of (s', rho0) in eval mode on the standardized composite test tensors; argmax and per-beat log-probabilities saved; same device and precision settings as the v2 trial (CUDA RTX 5060, deterministic, TF32 off)
computation.metric: Per seed bacc and Adv on the test part; Adv_composite(s -> s') = mean over the 3 seeds
computation.outputs: Composite test predictions and log-probabilities per seed and per (s, s') are saved with the test rows and labels (input of part d)

part_b_B_composite.reproduction_gate: Before any composite number: for every loaded target attacker, its predictions on the genuine u_s' test tensors must equal the saved pred_seed<seed> arrays of the v2 trial npz (s' in {2, 4, 5, 8}) or of part a (s' in {9, 10}) element for element. Any difference stops the run before a composite number exists; the difference is reported to SV1
part_b_B_composite.Pi_v3: Pi_v3(s, rho0) = 1 - max(Adv_naive(s), max over s' of Adv_composite(s -> s')), with Adv_naive(s) read from the v2 trial (s in {0, 2, 4, 5, 8}) or part a (s9, s0c). The CI95 is the v2 bootstrap applied to the predictions of the winning variant. Every variant's Adv, Pi, seed range and session bacc are reported
part_b_B_composite.unmeasured_splits: s1, s3, s6, s7 are not evaluated; no Pi is stated for them

reading_declared_before_run.role: Part b does not decide a branch: the no_signal branch is already taken (SV1 2026-11-19 section 3). It replaces the trial ordering with the upper bound the paper may state and tests the composite argument
reading_declared_before_run.argument_holds: Pi_v3(s, rho0) close to min over s' >= s of Pi_naive(s', rho0) at every source: the paper writes that splitting under rho0 does not hide the patient at any measured s, with Pi as an upper bound
reading_declared_before_run.argument_fails: If quantization or reduction at s makes a composite clearly weaker than B_naive at s' (Adv_composite well below Adv_naive(s')), report the numbers as they are; Pi_v3 still takes the max over variants and stays an upper bound

k_beat_vote.use: Part d (rho0, discussion) and the part c pass condition (k = 10)

modes.consecutive: Per patient, the test beats in time order cut into non-overlapping blocks of k consecutive beats; a last block shorter than k is dropped
modes.scattered: Per patient, 200 draws of k test beats without replacement, numpy.random.default_rng(numpy.random.SeedSequence([20261120, 4, pair_key, k])) with pair_key the index of the evaluated (configuration, split, alpha_t) in the run manifest written before the first draw, as when a policy offloads only part of the beats. The same blocks and draws are used by every aggregator

aggregators.hard: Majority of the per-beat argmax predictions in a block or draw (ties: lowest label)
aggregators.soft: Argmax of the sum of the per-beat log-probabilities in a block or draw. Needs saved log-probabilities: available for every new attacker of v3, not for the v2 trial pairs (receipt b2861c71 stores argmax only)
aggregators.mean: The k dequantized observed tensors of the block or draw (beats are R-peak aligned windows) are averaged element-wise (float64 accumulation, cast to float32) without re-quantization at the source. Source-level attackers receive the averaged tensor directly after their own standardization; composite paths compute u_s' from the averaged source tensor through the frozen ops (part b computation, re-quantized at s') and apply the attacker at s'. One prediction per block or draw and per seed. With independent per-beat noise the noise variance of the average is 1/k of a single beat (SV1 2026-11-25 item 1(1))

mean_attackers.rho0: Under rho0 (part d) the variants are those of Pi_v3: B_naive at the source and every B_composite s -> s', using the saved v2 or part a attackers (gate-checked) and observed tensors recomputed by v2 observed_tensor (or s0c_observed_tensor)
mean_attackers.noisy_configurations: Under part c: every variant of the configuration (B_naive, B_adaptive, every B_composite_adaptive s'), plus the clean rho0 attacker of the same source (the v2 trial s2-rho0 attackers for R2; the part a s0c-rho0 attackers for C0c), plus, for composite paths, the clean rho0 attackers at s' (v2 trial or part a). The averaged tensor is close to the clean distribution, so the clean attackers are included (SV1 2026-11-25 item 1(1); the clean attackers at s' are SV3's addition, cost only inference)

k_beat_vote.statistic: Per seed: bacc_k = mean over the N patients of the fraction of the patient's blocks or draws assigned to the right identity; Adv_k = clip((bacc_k - 1/N) / (1 - 1/N), 0, 1); mean over the 3 seeds; seed range reported
k_beat_vote.Pi_k: Pi_k = 1 - max over the attackers available for the evaluated configuration, the aggregators {hard, soft, mean} where available and the two modes, of the mean-seed Adv_k; every (attacker, aggregator, mode) value is reported
k_beat_vote.CI95: Consecutive mode: within-patient bootstrap over the k-beat blocks, 2000 resamples, identity set fixed, on the winning (attacker, aggregator); scattered mode: the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles over the 200 draws are reported instead of a bootstrap
k_beat_vote.difference_from_session_bacc: The consecutive k = 10 value can differ from the v2 session bacc, which kept the shorter last block

part_c_rho2_and_s0c_noise_control.status: Specification confirmed in principle by SV1 on 2026-11-25; runs only after the lock of this revision; DS1, results delivered on 2026-12-11 (H9), within 1.5 person-weeks counted from the lock (SV1 2026-11-25 section 0; guidance weeks 11-24, section 3.1 item 9)

configurations.R2[alpha]: s2 + rho2: on the device, z_s2 of checkpoint A plus Gaussian noise e[c, l] ~ N(0, (alpha * sigma_c)^2), independent per beat, channel and position, then registry v2 quantization; the edge dequantizes and runs the frozen tail
configurations.C0c[alpha]: The control: the 46 reduced values v = reduce46(x) (S0c v1 step 2) plus Gaussian noise N(0, (alpha * sigma_v)^2) per value, independent per beat, then S0c v1 steps 3-4 (quantize, rice_encode); the edge decodes, interpolates to 360 samples and runs the whole frozen model (SV1 2026-11-25 item 1(3); supplement item 2)
configurations.sigma: sigma_c = population std over N and L of channel c of the clean z_s2 of checkpoint A on DS1 train; sigma_v = population std over N and the 46 positions of the clean reduced values on DS1 train. Computed once and written to a file with its SHA-256 before any noisy evaluation. alpha only parametrizes each configuration; the configurations are compared at equal macro-F1, never at equal alpha
configurations.not_run: No full-length control on the 360-sample beat (SV1 2026-11-25 item 1(3))

part_c_rho2_and_s0c_noise_control.model: Checkpoint A frozen: no retraining of head or tail (ASI direction v3 section 2)

noise_generator.fixed_draws: numpy.random.default_rng(numpy.random.SeedSequence([20261120, config_index, alpha_key, part_index, draw])) with config_index 0 = R2, 2 = C0c (1 is not used); alpha_key = round(alpha * 1e6); part_index 1 attacker-validation, 2 test, 3 DS1 validation; draws 0, 1, 2 for utility; draw 0 for attacker-validation and test
noise_generator.fresh_training_noise: Attacker-train noise is drawn fresh for every epoch: numpy.random.default_rng(numpy.random.SeedSequence([20261120, config_index, alpha_key, 0, epoch])) generates one noise array for the whole attacker-train set in its fixed row order, so the noise of a beat does not depend on the batch order; epochs count from 1. Used by B_adaptive, A1_adaptive and B_composite_adaptive (SV1 2026-11-25 item 1(4))
noise_generator.fallback: Only if a timing of the full fresh-noise plan on random arrays (no MITDB) shows that part c would exceed the route R cap: at least 20 pre-drawn realizations (epoch e uses realization (e - 1) mod R, R >= 20), with R and the timing written to the run manifest before the first fit and reported to SV1
noise_generator.DS2: Official DS2 privacy round, same SeedSequence form [20261120, config_index, alpha_key, part_index, ...]: part_index 4 utility on DS2 (draws 0, 1, 2; data = every DS2 beat under the rules of the quality round), 5 attacker-validation on DS2 (draw 0), 6 test on DS2 (draw 0), 7 fresh attacker-train noise on DS2 per epoch (in place of 0). Every DS1 stream is unchanged and no DS2 stream equals a DS1 stream (SV1 2026-11-26 item 2(c))

utility.data: DS1 validation (as NoPeek v2 utility; the 4 validation records of the DS1/DS2 split); DS2 never used
utility.metric: Macro-F1 over N, S, V, F (fixed4), argmax over 5 outputs, zero_division 0, from the confusion summed over the 3 noise draws, exact with Fraction; per-draw macro-F1 and accuracy also reported
utility.gate: Passes when macro-F1 >= 19/20 x F1_A = 218290747091/404383914000 (0.5398), the threshold of route R and of rho1
utility.payload_size: C0c only: Rice body bytes per beat, len(rice_encode(q)), mean, median and maximum on DS1 validation at every alpha evaluated (the FP16 scale adds 2 B; the I1 envelope is fixed in contract I1). Reported for the cost comparison in G5; decides nothing here

matched_utility_search.targets: t in {0.99, 0.98, 0.97, 0.95} x F1_A; the last target is the gate (ASI direction v3 section 2)
matched_utility_search.rule: For each configuration and target t, utility only on the coarse grid; then bisection in log(alpha) between the largest grid alpha with macro-F1 >= t and the next grid alpha, 8 steps; alpha_t = the largest alpha found with macro-F1 >= t. If even 0.05 fails t, alpha_t is searched downward to 0.05/2^8; if no alpha reaches t, the target is reported unreachable. If macro-F1 is not monotone on the grid, the first crossing from small alpha is used and the non-monotone points are reported
matched_utility_search.selection_data: DS1 validation only; selecting alpha on DS1 validation is allowed (DS2 stays closed and unused)
matched_utility_search.privacy_points: Pi and Pi_k10 are evaluated at alpha_t of each reachable target for each configuration: at most 8 privacy points (4 targets x 2 configurations), at least 4 levels per configuration

privacy.data: v2 trial data and time split (DS1, N = 22)
privacy.attacker_knowledge: The attacker knows the mechanism, the checkpoint and alpha and sigma, can draw fresh noise from the known distribution at no cost (SV1 2026-11-25 item 1(4)), and holds labelled clean attacker-side beats of the N patients as in v2

variants.B_naive: Base architecture at the source (s2 for R2: NCL on [16, 180]; s0c for C0c: NCL on [1, 46]), trained on one noisy realization (draw 0 of part_index 0, i.e. epoch 0 of the fresh-noise generator) of the attacker-train tensors
variants.B_adaptive: Same architecture, trained with fresh noise every epoch (noise_generator.fresh_training_noise)
variants.B_composite_adaptive: For each s' in {2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10} deeper than the source: the edge computes u_s' from the noisy observed tensor (part b computation, frozen checkpoint A; for C0c from the interpolated x_c); a base-architecture attacker at s' is trained on the same pipeline applied to freshly noised attacker-train tensors, recomputed every epoch. Training-time composites run on the GPU (CUDA, deterministic, TF32 off) for speed; attacker-validation and test composites use the CPU computation of part b; the difference is floating-point rounding only. Standardization statistics from the epoch-1 realization of its own attacker-train part

privacy.seeds_and_training: Every variant: 3 seeds 20261030, 20261031, 20261101, v2 training settings (AdamW, early stop on attacker-validation bacc with the fixed draw-0 validation tensors, patience 5, max 50 epochs, TF32 off). Per-beat test log-probabilities are saved with the argmax predictions
privacy.Pi: Pi(config, alpha) = 1 - max over the variants of the mean-seed Adv (v2 privacy_metric); CI95 by the v2 bootstrap on the winning variant; every variant reported
privacy.Pi_k10: k_beat_vote.Pi_k at k = 10 over the attackers listed in k_beat_vote.mean_attackers.noisy_configurations, the three aggregators and both modes; from saved test predictions, log-probabilities and the fixed draw-0 test tensors; no further training. The other k values are reported as curves
privacy.variant_count: Per privacy point: 2 + 5 = 7 trained variants for R2, 2 + 6 = 8 for C0c, each with 3 seeds

reconstruction.why: The leakage budget Y protects ECG content, so the reconstruction at each noise level is reported with Pi (ASI direction v3 section 2)
reconstruction.floor: Training-free: R2 none (no identity map from z_s2); C0c: the edge interpolation x_c of the noisy reduced values
reconstruction.A1_adaptive: Trained at the source with fresh noise every epoch, MSE against the clean normalized x, seed 20261030, v2 A1 training settings. R2: v2 A1_decoder s2 mirror; C0c: the part a s0c refiner on x_c
reconstruction.metrics: v2 reconstruction_metrics (NRMSE, Pearson, R-peak error) on the draw-0 noisy test tensors, for the floor and for A1_adaptive; the headline is the better of the two by attacker-validation NRMSE

action_set_rules_declared_before_run.pass_on_DS1: A configuration is selected on DS1 at alpha when Pi(config, alpha) >= 0.5 and Pi_k10(config, alpha) >= 0.5 (point estimates, strongest attacker, aggregator and mode) and macro-F1 >= the gate
action_set_rules_declared_before_run.control_selected: If C0c is selected at some alpha: S0c + noise is preferred to s2 + rho2, whatever R2 gives; both privacy-utility curves are reported; report to SV1 at once
action_set_rules_declared_before_run.only_R2_selected: If no C0c alpha is selected and R2 is selected at some alpha: s2 + rho2 is the candidate; SV1 then measures its energy and latency and compares it with the S0c/S10 alternation policy at the same requirement (ASI direction v3 section 2); report to SV1 at once
action_set_rules_declared_before_run.neither: Otherwise: negative result for the mechanism and the range tried, with the per-beat Pi, Pi_k10 and the matched-F1 curves of both configurations; the leakage indicator stays in the system evaluation
action_set_rules_declared_before_run.DS2_confirmation: A selected configuration enters the action set only if the official DS2 privacy round (week 14, N = 21) also gives, as point estimates, Pi >= 0.5, Pi_k10 >= 0.5 and macro-F1_DS2(configuration, alpha) >= 19/20 x macro-F1_DS2(A, FP32), with the denominator taken from the DS2 quality round of 2026-12-10 (fixed before the privacy round), computed as an exact Fraction with the fixed4 metric; absolute macro-F1 values and CI95 are reported in the paper. On DS2 the attackers are the same recipe, not the same trained models: the same variants, architectures, training settings, seeds, aggregators and the alpha chosen on DS1, retrained on the attacker-train part of the 21 DS2 patients. If DS2 fails, the configuration is withdrawn and the result reported as it is (SV1 2026-11-25 item 1(5); SV1 2026-11-26 items 2(a) and 2(b))
action_set_rules_declared_before_run.comparison: At every reachable target t: Pi, Pi_k10 and the reconstruction metrics of R2 and C0c at alpha_t, with CI95 and per-attacker values, side by side at equal macro-F1
action_set_rules_declared_before_run.decision_time: SV1 decides routes R and K and the auxiliary model on 2026-12-13 with these rules (SV1 2026-11-25 section 0 and section 2)

part_c_rho2_and_s0c_noise_control.not_measured: E_prot of the noise generation on the nRF52840 (SV1 2026-11-19 section 8); the energy comparison of a selected configuration belongs to G5 v2

part_d_k_beats_rho0.question: How many beats of one patient must the edge see before it re-identifies the patient? Supports the threat-model statement that the leakage budget Y does not hide identity
part_d_k_beats_rho0.inputs: Saved per-beat test predictions and log-probabilities, recomputed observed tensors and saved attackers only, no training: the v2 trial predictions and attackers (read, never edited) and the part a and part b outputs. For each measured s under rho0 (and s0c) the attackers of Pi_v3(s, rho0); s0c is the primary row
part_d_k_beats_rho0.computation: k_beat_vote over all k_values, both modes, aggregators hard (every row), soft (where log-probabilities exist) and mean (every row)
part_d_k_beats_rho0.status: Discussion only under rho0, never Pi and never a decision rule

official_DS2_privacy_round.when: Week 14 (2026-12-14 to 2026-12-20), after the quality round of 2026-12-10, under its own authorization file provided by the user
official_DS2_privacy_round.scope: Parts a, b and d of this revision on the DS2 patients (N = 21, record 202 excluded, v2 official-round data rules), including B_composite, s9/s10 and S0c, plus any configuration selected by part c on DS1 with its alpha and attackers. Each locked configuration is evaluated on DS2 once
official_DS2_privacy_round.not_in_scope: No choice of any parameter (alpha, k, threshold, configuration, seed) is made on DS2
official_DS2_privacy_round.DS2_macro_F1_rule: Every macro-F1 gate on DS2 is relative to A on DS2: 19/20 x macro-F1_DS2(A, FP32) from the quality round of 2026-12-10, exact Fraction, fixed4. The rule applies to every action and every path (FP32, INT8/FP16, DPU, S0c), so this protocol and the LUT use one rule (SV1 2026-11-26 item 2(c))

constraints: The 9 pairs of the v2 trial are never rerun or edited; their files are read only and checked against receipt b2861c71
DS2 is not opened by any DS1 part of this version; the official DS2 privacy round needs its own authorization
Pi_min = 0.5, the Pi formula, the attack models, the data split and the capacity decision are those of v2
Trial numbers stay an early warning and never enter the paper's main numbers
No S0c number exists before the runner reproduces S0c v1 bit for bit (s0c_observed_tensor.implementation)
run_order_after_lock: Part a: golden checks s9, s10 and the S0c reproduction check; B_naive and A1 at s9, s10, then s0c; report Pi_v3(s9), Pi_logits and Pi(s0c) the day they exist
Part b: v2 receipt check, reproduction gate, then the 27 composite evaluations; report the Pi_v3 table
Part d: from the saved predictions, recomputed observed tensors and saved attackers of the v2 trial and parts a and b; report with the Pi_v3 table. Parts a, b, d delivered on 2026-12-06 (H8)

Part c: sigma file first, then the matched-utility search and payload sizes (DS1 validation), then the privacy points (Pi, Pi_k10, reconstruction); delivered on 2026-12-11 (H9), within the route R cap counted from the lock
limitations: v2 limitations apply (N = 21 official, no sex/age inference, trial on DS1 patients seen in training)

Closed-set re-identification of N patients with attacker train and test from two halves of the same record: identity is confounded with session features (electrodes, posture), so Adv is higher than for cross-session re-identification; MIT-BIH has one session per patient and cannot separate the two

Direction of the bounds: with respect to attacker strength every measured Pi is an upper bound of the in-session Pi; with respect to the session confound the in-session Adv is an upper bound of the cross-session Adv (the in-session Pi a lower bound of the cross-session Pi). The negative result is therefore stated for the in-session closed-set task
The edge already knows which device sends; the threat is linking beats to an identity in another dataset or session, of which the in-session Adv is an upper bound

Leakage budget Y (ASI direction v3 sections 3 and changes table): Y is the fraction of beats processed fully on the device (>= p); it limits how much ECG content leaves the device and does not hide identity, since a few beats of one session re-identify the patient (part d). Pi per beat, Pi_k and the reconstruction metrics are reported separately and are not weights of Y

Aggregation across beats: Pi_k uses majority, soft and mean aggregation over fixed attackers. Learned multi-beat attackers (trained on sets of beats) and alignment refinements beyond the R-peak window are not tested, so Pi_k stays an upper bound with respect to stronger aggregation
KV260 INT8 logits are not attacked; B_composite and part a cover rho0 only

rho2 and C0c are evaluated with checkpoint A frozen (no noise-aware fine-tune); Pi for them is an upper bound with respect to stronger adaptive attackers (for example denoising networks); a stronger reconstruction attack (A2 with a discriminator) is run only if a configuration is selected (guidance weeks 11-24, section 5.2)
S0c results hold for S0C-V1 only; another reduction or interpolation needs a new measurement
